HOW IT WORKS

The Meme Fast Model

Meme Fast is a research dashboard for meme and token markets. It connects public attention, exact token contracts, market screening, and observed swaps so you can investigate what happened. This is a research model, not a price-prediction model.

ONE VIEW OF THE WORKFLOW

The toolsRead order flowData methodLimits

Five questions, five places to investigate

The workflow is a way to narrow a question, not a sequence that a coin must pass through. You can start with a story, a contract address, or an observed market move.

  1. Tweet / Narrative What is attracting attention?

    Public news headlines and sampled pool activity surface possible stories. Related names and cashtags are leads. An exact contract link is stronger evidence, but neither proves a project is authentic.

  2. Snipe Which new pools deserve a closer look?

    New-pool candidates are screened by age, liquidity, transactions, short-window flow, and available story context. Launchpad completion, volume-only migration candidates, and observed recovery patterns are shown separately. A screen pass is not a live execution or safety check.

  3. Swing Which observed coins deserve research time?

    Separate short-horizon and multi-day rankings compare available turnover, liquidity, activity, persistence, and context. Scores order a sampled research queue; they do not estimate returns. Missing or stale inputs are exposed, and incomplete snapshots can withhold a score.

  4. Inspect What do the observed swaps actually show?

    Choose an exact listing and look at buy and sell value, net observed flow, swap sizes, and estimated market-cap tiers. Inspect is useful for seeing whether activity is concentrated in small or large swaps and where it appeared along the valuation range. It is not a complete transaction history.

  5. Watchlist What should I revisit?

    Save narratives and exact tokens to a research queue in your own browser. The list is local to that browser; it is neither a public portfolio nor a recommendation.

How to read an Inspect result

Search a ticker to compare returned listings, or paste an exact contract to narrow the identity. Check the chain and pool coverage before interpreting the numbers. Then move from the summary to the trend, size bands, and individual swap steps.

Buy / sell volumeUSD value of returned swaps classified on each side for the selected window.
Net flowObserved buy value minus observed sell value. It is not total capital inflow.
Swap stepsReturned swap events, not a count of distinct people or wallets.
Flow trendBuy and sell value by interval. It is not a cumulative net-flow series.
Size and MC tiersWhere returned activity sits by USD swap size and estimated execution market cap.
Latest swapsInspect transaction steps, pools, and sender addresses; a sender can be a router or smart account.

One large buy is one observation, not confirmation of sustained demand. Compare it with surrounding swaps, liquidity, pool coverage, and the time window. Large activity can reflect routing, arbitrage, bots, or other mechanics; the view cannot establish intent or identify wash trading.

Where the data comes from

Separate a story from a contract

Public news feeds supply headlines; sampled indexed X posts offer incomplete social context. GeckoTerminal and DEX Screener supply pool and token lookups, while GeckoTerminal supplies the swaps shown in Inspect. Meme Fast groups candidate headlines and looks for evidence connecting a story to a token. A shared name, ticker, alias, or cashtag can suggest a lead; only evidence identifying the exact contract earns an exact-contract label. This distinction matters because different tokens can share a name.

Compare like with like

Snipe retains a bounded set of discovered pools and applies explicit screens. Swing ranks a sampled universe using the inputs available for its chosen horizon. Both show coverage and freshness because a missing value is unknown, not zero. Pool creation is not necessarily token creation, and pool volume is not token-wide volume. Snipe is a discovery screen, not a buy signal; Swing scores are research priority, not return forecasts.

Pool coverage and flow calculations

A token can trade in several pools. Inspect discovers up to three of the most liquid returned pools for a selected listing and requests up to 300 recent swaps per pool from the past 24 hours. Smaller or unindexed pools can be absent, so displayed totals can be incomplete. It deduplicates returned events and groups swap steps from one transaction without turning them into a trader's net cash movement. Its size bands are S under $100, M $100–under $1,000, L $1,000–under $10,000, and XL $10,000 or more. Net flow is observed buy USD value minus observed sell USD value.

Estimated market-cap tiers use swap execution price and a supply inferred from the latest reported market cap and price, assuming supply has not changed. The separate five-day view uses completed candles from one discovered pool; candle volume is assigned to a tier by closing market cap, and candles cannot supply a buy/sell split. These calculations make the data easier to inspect while preserving their sampling limits. For the full calculation details, open Inspect and expand “Data coverage & calculation.” See Sources for current feed coverage.

What this evidence cannot tell you

Market data can be delayed, unavailable, or limited to the pools and swaps returned by providers. Public news and indexed social posts are incomplete measures of attention. A transaction sender can be a router or smart account, not an individual buyer. Estimated market cap depends on a supply assumption, and market cap and liquidity can change quickly. None of these views verifies contract permissions, ownership, sellability, execution price, or token safety.

High observed buy volume does not guarantee a price rise. The dashboard cannot determine trader intent, distinguish every bot or arbitrage route, or establish that activity is organic. We use these signals to decide what to inspect next, not to predict a price or endorse a trade.

An example research pass

Start with an exact token contract. Check the chain and returned pools, inspect liquidity and data freshness, compare buy and sell value in the selected window, look across swap sizes and recent transactions, then return to the source coverage and any narrative evidence. Save it to your browser-local Watchlist if it merits another look. This is research and education, not financial advice; do your own research before any decision.
